crop.notes: Allen's letter is complete, but the Boston Herald item below continues at the top of the next column and is cut off mid-sentence. crop-2 is blank paper.

summary.suggested: The St. Louis Globe-Democrat reprinted Tom Allen's letter to the New York Herald, written on his return from six years in England, challenging John L. Sullivan or any man to fight for $1,000 to $5,000 a side and the championship of the world.

metadata.notes: Masthead: St. Louis Daily Globe-Democrat, Monday Morning, November 6, 1882

facts.fact: Allen returned to America after six years in England, where he had kept a standing challenge to fight any man in Great Britain
Allen wrote that he held the heavyweight championship until his fight with Joe Goss in 1876
facts.quote: which title I held until my battle with Joe Goss in 1876

facts.fact: Allen challenged John L. Sullivan or any man in the world, London prize ring rules, catch weight, for $1,000 or $5,000 a side and the championship of the world, the fight within three months within 100 miles of New Orleans; his backer posted $1,000 and Harry Hill was to be final stakeholder
facts.quote: I will fight John L. Sullivan or any man in the world, according to the rules of the London prize ring, at catch weight, for $1,000 or $5,000 a side and the championship of the world.

facts.fact: Richard K. Fox's representative arrived in Boston with full power to match Allen against Sullivan for $2,500 a side; Sullivan's backer named November 10 to sign articles but said Sullivan would not fight in New Orleans
